title: The founder of peace, not faction
source_text: Ἐπεὶ δέ φησι πάλιν ὁ Κέλσος ὅτι, εἰ διδάξαις αὐτοὺς ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν οὗτος ἐκείνου παῖς, ἀλλ᾿ ἐκεῖνός γε πάντων πατὴρ, ὃν μόνον ὡς ἀληθῶς δεῖ σέβειν· οὐκ ἂν ἔτι θέλοιεν, εἰ μὴ καὶ τοῦτον, ὅσπερ ἐστὶν αὐτοῖς τῆς στάσεως ἀρχηγέτης. καὶ ὠνόμασάν γε τοῦτον θεοῦ υἱὸν, οὐχ ὅτι τὸν θεὸν σφόδρα σέβουσιν, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι τοῦτον σφόδρα αὔξουσιν, ἡμεῖς μὲν οὖν μαθόντες, τίς ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ὅτι „ἀπαύγασμά“ ἐστι „τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ“ καὶ „ἀτμὶς“ μὲν „τῆς θεοῦ δυνάμεως ἀπόῤῥοια δὲ τῆς τοῦ παντοκράτορος δόξης εἰλικρινὴς“ ἔτι δὲ „ἀπαύγασμα“ „φωτὸς ἀϊδίου καὶ ἔσοπτρον ἀκηλίδωτον τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἐνεργείας καὶ εἰκὼν τῆς ἀγαθότητος αὐτοῦ,“ ἴσμεν ὅτι οὗτος υἱὸς ἐξ ἐκείνου, καὶ ἐκεῖνος τούτου πατήρ. καὶ οὐδὲν ἀπρεπές ἐστιν ἐν τῷ λόγῳ οὐδὲ ἀνάρμοστον θεῷ, τοιοῦτον υἱὸν μονογενῆ ὑφιστάντι. καὶ οὐκ ἂν μεταπείσηταί τις ἡμᾶς ὅτι οὐχ υἱὸς ὁ τοιοῦτος τοῦ ἀγεννήτου θεοῦ ἐστι καὶ πατρός. εἰ δέ τινων παρήκουσε Κέλσος, μὴ ὁμολογούντων τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ υἱὸν εἶναι τοῦ δημιουργήσαντος τόδε τὸ πᾶν, αὐτὸς ἂν εἰδείη καὶ οἱ συγκατατιθέμενοι τοιούτῳ λόγῳ. οὐ στάσεως οὖν ἀρχηγέτης ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀλλὰ πάσης εἰρήνης. ὁ εἰπὼν τοῖς μαθηταῖς· „εἰρήνην ἀφίημι ὑμῖν, εἰρήνην τὴν ἐμὴν δίδωμι ὑμῖν.“ εἶτ᾿ ἐπείπερ ἠπίστατο τοὺς τοῦ κόσμου καὶ οὐ θεοῦ ἀνθρώπους προσπολεμήσοντας ἡμῖν, προσέθηκεν ἐκείνοις τὸ „οὐ καθὼς ὁ κόσμος δίδωσιν εἰρήνην, κἀγὼ δίδωμι ὑμῖν εἰρήνην.“ θαῤῥοῦμεν δὲ δι᾿ αὐτὸν, κἂν θλιβώμεθα ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, εἰπόντα· „ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ θλῖψιν ἔχετε· ἀλλὰ θαρσεῖτε, ἐγὼ νενίκηκα τὸν κόσμον.“ καὶ τοῦτόν φαμεν εἶναι υἱὸν θεοῦ· θεοῦ δὲ, ὃν, εἰ δεῖ ταῖς λέξεσιν ἀκολουθῆσαι Κέλσου, σφόδρα σέβομεν, καὶ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ σφόδρα ηὐξημένον ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς γινώσκομεν. ἔστω δέ τινας ὡς ἐν πλήθει πιστευόντων καὶ δεχομένων διαφωνίαν διὰ τὴν προπέτειαν ὑποτίθεσθαι τὸν σωτῆρα εἶναι τὸν μέγιστον ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεὸν, ἀλλ᾿ οὔτι γε ἡμεῖς τοιοῦτο (ν. οἱ) πειθόμενοι αὐτῷ λέγοντι· „ὁ πατὴρ ὁ πέμψας με μείζων μου ἐστί“· διόπερ (οὐ) χ ὅν νῦν πατέρα καλοῦμεν ὑποβάλοιμεν (ἂν) . ὡς Κέλσος ἡμᾶς συκοφαντῶν (φησι) , τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ θεοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: But since Celsus says again that 'if you were to teach (διδάξαις) them that this one is not that one's child (παῖς), but that that one is Father of all, whom alone one must truly (ὡς ἀληθῶς) revere (σέβειν), they would no longer be willing, unless also this one, who is for them the founder/leader (ἀρχηγέτης) of the faction (στάσεως). And they named him Son of God, not because they greatly (σφόδρα) revere God, but because they greatly exalt/magnify (αὔξουσιν) this one.' We then, having learned who the Son of God is, and that He is 'radiance (ἀπαύγασμα) of the glory and imprint (χαρακτήρ) of His hypostasis (ὑποστάσεως)' and 'vapour/breath (ἀτμίς) of the power of God, and pure (εἰλικρινής) emanation (ἀπόρροια) of the glory of the Almighty (παντοκράτορος)', and further 'radiance of eternal (ἀϊδίου) light and spotless (ἀκηλίδωτον) mirror (ἔσοπτρον) of the working (ἐνεργείας) of God and image of His goodness (ἀγαθότητος)', we know that this one is Son from that one, and that one Father of this one. And there is nothing unseemly (ἀπρεπές) in the teaching (λόγῳ), nor unfitting (ἀνάρμοστον) for God, who causes to subsist (ὑφιστάντι) such an only-begotten Son. And no one would persuade us otherwise (μεταπείσηται) that such a one is not Son of the unbegotten (ἀγεννήτου) God and Father. But if Celsus heard/overheard (παρήκουσε) some not confessing (ὁμολογούντων) the Son of God to be Son of the one who crafted (δημιουργήσαντος) this universe, he himself would know [it], and those assenting (συγκατατιθέμενοι) to such teaching. Not then founder of faction is Jesus but of all peace (εἰρήνης), He who said to the disciples: 'peace I leave (ἀφίημι) to you, my peace I give to you.' Then since He knew that the men of the world (κόσμου) and not of God would war against (προσπολεμήσοντας) us, He added to those the 'not as the world gives peace, I also give you peace.' And we take courage (θαρροῦμεν) through Him, even if we are afflicted (θλιβώμεθα) in the world, who said: 'in the world you have affliction (θλῖψιν); but take courage, I have conquered (νενίκηκα) the world.' And this one we say is Son of God; of God, whom, if we must follow the words (λέξεσιν) of Celsus, we greatly revere, and we know His Son greatly exalted (ηὐξημένον) by the Father. Let it be (ἔστω) that some, as in a multitude (πλήθει) of believers and admitting disagreement (διαφωνίαν), through rashness (προπέτειαν) suppose (ὑποτίθεσθαι) the Saviour to be the greatest God over all; but not we, obeying Him saying: 'the Father who sent me is greater (μείζων) than I'; wherefore we would not subject (ὑποβάλοιμεν) the One we now call Father, as Celsus slandering (συκοφαντῶν) us says, to the Son of God.
pass_b_english: Celsus says again: “If you were to teach them that this man is not His child, but that He is the Father of all, who alone ought truly to be revered, they would no longer be willing, unless they were to revere this man too, who is the founder of their faction. And they called him Son of God not because they revere God greatly, but because they exalt this man greatly.”

We, however, have learned who the Son of God is: that He is “the radiance of the glory and the imprint of His being” (Hebrews 1:3), and “a breath of the power of God, and a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty” (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25), and again “the radiance of eternal light, and a spotless mirror of the working of God, and an image of His goodness” (Wisdom of Solomon 7:26). So we know that He is the Son who comes from God, and that God is His Father. And there is nothing unseemly in this teaching, nor anything unfitting for God, who gives existence to such an only-begotten Son. No one could persuade us that such a one is not the Son of the unbegotten God and Father. If Celsus has heard some people who do not confess that the Son of God is the Son of the One who made this universe, that is a matter for him and for those who agree with such teaching.

Jesus, then, is the founder not of faction but of all peace. He said to the disciples, “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you” (John 14:27). Then, since He knew that men of the world and not of God would make war on us, He added to those words, “Not as the world gives peace do I give you peace” (John 14:27). And even if we are afflicted in the world, we take courage because of Him who said, “In the world you have affliction; but take courage, I have overcome the world” (John 16:33).

He is the One we say is the Son of God; of God, whom, if we must follow Celsus’s wording, we revere greatly; and we know that His Son has been greatly exalted by the Father. Grant that some, as may happen in a multitude of believers who admit differences of opinion, rashly suppose that the Saviour is the supreme God over all. We do not; for we obey Him when He says, “The Father who sent me is greater than I” (John 14:28). That is why we would not subject Him whom we now call Father to the Son of God, as Celsus falsely accuses us of doing.

choices.choice: Celsus’s words run to σφόδρα αὔξουσιν. In his mouth ‘His child’ and ‘He is the Father’ refer to the supreme God, so those pronouns are capitalised; ‘this man’ / ‘him’ for Jesus stay lower-case. ‘Unless they were to revere this man too’ supplies the verb implied by εἰ μὴ καὶ τοῦτον. ἀρχηγέτης is rendered ‘founder’ in both Celsus’s charge and Origen’s reply, to keep Origen’s turn of the word. Hebrews 1:3 χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως rendered ‘imprint of His being’, as in 8.12. Wisdom of Solomon 7:25-26 is quoted closely; ἀτμίς rendered ‘breath’. John 14:27b: Origen’s form ‘Not as the world gives peace do I also give you peace’ (κἀγὼ) differs slightly from the usual text; ‘also’ is dropped as redundant in English. First-person pronouns in Christ’s own words stay lower-case, as elsewhere in this chunk. John 14:28 is quoted with ‘who sent me’, as also in 8.15; the usual text reads ‘the Father is greater than I’. ‘Greatly exalted by the Father’ may echo Philippians 2:9 (not cited, uncertain). The end of the chapter is damaged in the staged text: (οὐ)χ ὅν ... ὑποβάλοιμεν (ἂν) ... (φησι) and τοιοῦτο(ν. οἱ) are editorial restorations; rendered as restored, with the negation ‘would not subject’. ‘The supreme God over all’ renders τὸν μέγιστον ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεόν (the greatest God over all). ‘That is a matter for him’ renders αὐτὸς ἂν εἰδείη (he himself would know).
'unless they could revere this man too' -> 'unless they were to revere this man too' (εἰ μὴ καὶ τοῦτον; removed added ability modal)
'the exact imprint of His being' -> 'the imprint of His being' (χαρακτήρ, as in 8.12)
'My peace' -> 'my peace' (lower-case first person in Christ's words, consistent with 'in me', 'sent me')
'the most high God over all' -> 'the supreme God over all' (μέγιστον, not the biblical title ὕψιστος)
checked Hebrews 1:3, Wisdom of Solomon 7:25-26, John 14:27, John 16:33, John 14:28 wording against the Greek
